sections.content: Savannah, Georgia doesn't get the same headlines as Atlanta or Charlotte, but savvy investors have been quietly building wealth here for years. The city blends stable rental demand, a booming tourism economy, and a port that drives consistent job growth — a combination that creates real opportunity across multiple investing strategies. Whether you're wholesaling, flipping, or building a rental portfolio, real estate deals in Savannah GA are worth serious attention in 2024. If you're just getting started, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in.
Savannah GA Real Estate Market Overview

Savannah sits in Chatham County along Georgia's Atlantic coast, and its economy is built on three strong pillars: the Port of Savannah (one of the busiest in the country), a thriving tourism industry drawing over 14 million visitors per year, and a growing presence of manufacturing and logistics companies. Major employers like Gulfstream Aerospace, JCB, and Hyundai's new EV plant in nearby Bryan County are pulling thousands of workers into the region, creating sustained housing demand that investors can capitalize on.

As of late 2024, the median home price in Savannah sits around $295,000 to $315,000, depending on the zip code and property type. That's well below the national median, which means your entry costs are lower and your rental yields can be more attractive. Days on market have stretched slightly compared to the 2021–2022 frenzy, averaging around 35 to 50 days in most neighborhoods. That cooldown is good news for investors — motivated sellers are easier to find, and there's more room to negotiate.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Savannah

Savannah is a city of distinct neighborhoods, and each one tells a different investing story. Understanding where the opportunity lives is the first step to building a profitable deal pipeline. You can explore active listings and neighborhood data directly on our [Savannah GA market page](aiwholesail.com/markets/savannah-ga).
Historic District and Victorian District

These are the crown jewels of Savannah real estate. Properties here command premium prices — often $450,000 to $1.2 million — but they also generate exceptional short-term rental income thanks to heavy tourist foot traffic. A well-renovated Victorian District row house can pull $200 to $350 per night on Airbnb during peak season. The flip opportunity here is real, but renovation costs are high due to historic preservation requirements. Budget carefully and always get contractor bids before making an offer.
Midtown and Ardsley Park

Midtown offers the best balance of price and potential for most investors. Median prices range from $200,000 to $320,000, and the neighborhood draws young professionals, SCAD students, and long-term residents alike. Ardsley Park is particularly strong for buy-and-hold investors who want stable, long-term tenants. Rental rates for a 3-bedroom home here typically run $1,600 to $2,100 per month, which pencils out nicely at current price points.
Eastside and Georgetown

These neighborhoods are where wholesalers and fix-and-flip investors find their best margins. Home prices often fall in the $120,000 to $210,000 range, with distressed properties available well below that. ARVs after renovation typically land between $220,000 and $290,000, giving flippers a workable spread if they buy right. These areas are also seeing steady infrastructure investment from the city, which bodes well for long-term appreciation.

Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Savannah
Wholesale Deals

Savannah has a healthy wholesale market, fueled by aging housing stock and a steady stream of motivated sellers dealing with probate, divorce, job relocation, or deferred maintenance. Typical wholesale assignment fees in Savannah range from $8,000 to $25,000 per deal, depending on the property's condition and location. If you're new to this strategy, start with our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide to understand the basics before building your Savannah pipeline.
Fix and Flip

Savannah's flipping market is active but competitive in the mid-tier price range. The sweet spot for flippers is buying in the $130,000 to $180,000 range in neighborhoods like Eastside or Georgetown, putting $40,000 to $65,000 into renovations, and reselling at $240,000 to $290,000. That structure can yield net profits of $30,000 to $55,000 per deal after carrying costs, assuming you buy right and manage the rehab efficiently. Historic properties require more budget — always account for potential lead paint, knob-and-tube wiring, and foundation work in older homes.
Long-Term Rentals

The rental market in Savannah is driven by port workers, military personnel from nearby Hunter Army Airfield, SCAD students, and healthcare workers at Memorial Health and St. Joseph's. Vacancy rates hover around 4 to 6 percent in most residential neighborhoods, which is healthy for landlords. Single-family homes in Midtown and Southside Savannah can achieve gross rental yields of 7 to 9 percent at current prices — strong numbers compared to many coastal markets.
Short-Term Rentals

Tourism in Savannah is a year-round engine, with peak season running spring through early fall. Savannah currently allows short-term rentals in most zones with proper licensing, though regulations have tightened in recent years. Well-positioned properties near Forsyth Park, River Street, or the Historic District can gross $35,000 to $75,000 annually as short-term rentals. Always verify current STR regulations with the City of Savannah before purchasing with this strategy in mind.
Key Market Trends Shaping Savannah Real Estate in 2024

items: Hyundai's EV manufacturing plant in nearby Bryan County is expected to bring 8,500+ direct jobs and tens of thousands of indirect jobs to the region, creating a wave of housing demand in surrounding communities
Port of Savannah expansion projects continue to attract logistics and warehousing companies, keeping industrial real estate hot and residential demand strong
Rising insurance costs in coastal Georgia are squeezing some landlord margins, making accurate expense modeling essential before you buy
Savannah's short-term rental market saw slight softening in 2023 but rebounded in 2024 as tourism continued to grow

Investor activity from out-of-state buyers — particularly from Florida, New York, and California — has increased, pushing up prices on turnkey properties but leaving distressed deals relatively untouched

Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Savannah is a popular target for out-of-state investors, and for good reason — prices are accessible, demand is diversified, and the market is large enough to find deals consistently. But investing remotely requires a solid local infrastructure. Here's how to set yourself up for success.

items: Build your local team first: Find a real estate attorney familiar with Georgia contracts, a reliable property manager charging 8 to 10 percent of monthly rent, and at least two licensed contractors you can trust to give accurate bids remotely

Focus on off-market deals: The best margins in Savannah come from properties that never hit the MLS. Learn how to source them in our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals)
Drive the market virtually: Use Google Street View, neighborhood walk-through videos on YouTube, and local Facebook investor groups to understand each micro-neighborhood before committing capital
Underwrite conservatively: Georgia's coastal location means higher insurance premiums. Budget 1.2 to 1.5 percent of home value annually for insurance, not the national average

Always analyze before you offer: Use a systematic framework to evaluate every deal. Our guide on [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) walks through the exact numbers to run before making any offer
Visit before you close: Even one trip to Savannah to walk target neighborhoods will sharpen your judgment more than hours of desktop research

sections.content: Pro Tip: Join the Savannah Real Estate Investors Association (REIA) or local BiggerPockets forums for the Savannah market. These communities are goldmines for finding wholesale deals, off-market properties, and vetted local contractors — especially valuable if you're investing from out of state.
Is Savannah the Right Market for You?

Savannah checks a lot of boxes for investors at multiple experience levels. Entry-level investors can find affordable distressed properties to wholesale or flip. Experienced landlords can build cash-flowing rental portfolios with solid yields. And investors chasing appreciation can position in neighborhoods benefiting from the regional economic boom. The market isn't perfect — insurance costs are rising, STR regulations can be tricky, and competition for turnkey deals is stiff. But for investors willing to do the work and buy intelligently, real estate deals in Savannah GA continue to offer compelling risk-adjusted returns compared to pricier coastal markets.
